headline: Don't build a harness benchmark engine: Harbor (plus Inspect for non-code tasks) already runs any harness on containerized tasks at scale. What nobody has built is the Azm layer on top: tasks mined from Azm's own repos, adapters for squad-kit and azm-harness, standards-compliance scoring, per-team YAML suites and a report people can act on.
bottomLine: Prior art exists and is recent: AWS published a harness-vs-model cost/quality benchmark on your own code (MIT-0, 21 Oct 2026); Fullscript ran 36 tasks mined from its own commits (Aug 2026); GitHub published its harness evaluation protocol (Jun 2026). Azm's sandbox should combine their methods, not reinvent them.
The harness matters more than the model: harness variance was 7.8x model variance in a 3x3 study, and the same model moved ~10 points on SWE-bench Pro between harnesses. That justifies the track.

Execution and isolation are solved problems: Harbor (Apache-2.0) for running agents on tasks; Docker locally, then E2B (self-host/BYOC) or Kubernetes agent-sandbox / OpenSandbox on Azm infrastructure.

squad-kit has no direct equivalent that covers spec → release with human gates and readable project memory, but Archon (YAML workflows, MIT) and AI-DLC (one core, seven harnesses) are close peers to benchmark against.
The real gap, unclaimed by any tool found: measuring harnesses on a company's own SDLC work, including standards compliance and non-code steps, with per-team configuration.

priorArt.name: AWS agentic coding harness benchmarks
priorArt.takes: Task mining from closed issues, 5 harnesses, LLM judge, cost/quality frontier, swe-router.
priorArt.lacks: Hidden tests, real sandbox, multi-team config, standards scoring.

priorArt.name: Fullscript internal benchmark
priorArt.takes: Fail-before/pass-after tasks from own commits, developer-value score, safety zeroing, LiteLLM gateway.
priorArt.lacks: Published code; per-team config; ongoing service.

priorArt.name: GitHub Copilot harness evaluation
priorArt.takes: Normalised comparisons, ≥5 runs with ±1σ, infra-failure policy.

priorArt.name: Harbor / Terminal-Bench
priorArt.takes: Agent-agnostic runner, containers, cloud parallelism, adapters.
priorArt.lacks: Azm tasks, standards scoring, org reporting.

priorArt.name: HarnessBench / WildClawBench
priorArt.takes: Fixed-model / varied-harness design, post-run grader injection.

architecture.detail: Mine 20-50 tasks per team from Azm repos and tickets: pinned commit before the fix, brief from the real ticket, hidden fail-before/pass-after tests, plus non-code tasks (spec, design, review) graded by rubric. Refresh quarterly to avoid saturation.
Run every harness × model on every task in parallel; inject graders only after the run.

architecture.use: Harbor BaseInstalledAgent; Rivet sandbox-agent as an option
architecture.detail: Adapters for squad-kit (needs a headless mode), azm-harness, Claude Code, Codex CLI, opencode, pi, and mini-swe-agent as the control.

architecture.use: Docker → E2B self-host/BYOC or k8s agent-sandbox / OpenSandbox
architecture.detail: Fixed, recorded CPU/memory/time per task (infra noise is ~6 pp otherwise); egress allow-lists; no production secrets.
Any harness to any model; per-team keys and budgets; cost per run.
Traces, tokens, cost, latency per run; transcripts for review.

architecture.use: Hidden tests + rubric judge + Track 1 rules
architecture.detail: Resolved, developer-value score (0-100), standards-compliance score from Track 1 checks, safety violations zero the run, pass^k over 3-5 runs.
suite.yaml per team: repos, tasks, harnesses, models, budgets, thresholds.
Harness × model × team matrix, cost/quality frontier, variance, trends; CI regression gate for harness or standard changes; a Harness Card per harness.

buildList: Task-mining pipeline (repo + ticket → task with hidden tests)
squad-kit headless mode and its Harbor adapter; azm-harness adapter
Report: matrix, frontier, variance, trends; weekly email/Teams summary
Regression gate in CI for harness/standard changes

phases.name: Week 1 — Pilot
items: 10 tasks mined from one Azm repo
Claude Code, Codex CLI, mini-swe-agent baselines

phases.name: Weeks 2-3 — Azm harnesses
items: Add Archon, AI-DLC, Superpowers as contenders

phases.name: Week 4 — Teams
items: Move runs to E2B or k8s sandbox

phases.name: Later
items: Harness and skill optimisation loops (Meta-Harness, auto-harness, SkillOpt)
Channel agents evaluated with Promptfoo red-team checks

risks: Task leakage: keep hidden tests out of the sandbox until grading.
Judge bias: prefer tests; calibrate the rubric judge against human scores.
Noise: fixed resources, ≥3 runs, report variance; don't rank on <5 pp gaps.
Licences: AGPL tools (Chorus, Trellis) and ELv2 (Phoenix) need care if embedded.
Data: managed sandboxes and hosted agents send code off Azm infrastructure; use self-host/BYOC for private repos.
decisions: Which 1-2 Azm repos supply the pilot tasks?
Docker on an Azm server first, or E2B managed for the pilot?
Does squad-kit get a headless mode (needed for automated runs)?
Budget ceiling per benchmark round (tokens + sandbox)?
